content:
**hooks keep the stream the tool speaks on (#633)**

Three hook lines discarded stderr on memory/cli.mjs invocations, so the duplicate report #598 deliberately put on stderr -- precisely so automated callers would keep it -- reached nobody on the push and post-merge paths.

Measured what each verb writes per stream instead of assuming: share 0 stdout / 3 stderr, reindex 1/3, feature-checkpoint 0 stdout / 2 stderr. That last one settles the line the ticket only suspected: `2>/dev/null` on feature-checkpoint discarded 100% of what the command says, and what it silenced is the hook's own documented A2 limitation announcing itself ("ambiguous active feature ... skipping checkpoint"). A limitation documented in a comment and invisible at runtime is indistinguishable from one that does not occur.

The sharper half is pre-push's tamper path. `|| exit 0` is deliberate and stays -- a tooling problem must not block a push -- but it discards the exit code by design, so once `2>&1` discarded the message there was NO channel left. Measured before/after on a planted tampered record: both exit 0, but before the operator saw 0 lines and now sees rebuildIndex's full id-mismatch refusal. Not blocking was the decision; being silent was not.

Prose was not enough and the file proves it: post-merge:35 already carried the correct reasoning in its own comment, and post-merge:43 carried `2>&1` eight lines below it. A rule that lives in one comment decays (#575's thesis, inside a single 46-line file). So the rule is stated in both headers AND enforced by a scan of every hook for cli.mjs invocations -- with no list of known lines, because a list passes forever while a fourth bad line is added beside them.

Two test layers because each catches what the other cannot: behavioural (run the REAL hooks with a mock node writing a distinct marker to each stream, following pre-push.test.mjs's technique) proves the redirection works; structural (scan every hook) covers the line somebody adds next year. The mock writes to BOTH streams unconditionally, since a stderr-only mock would pass against a hook that also discarded stdout.

Corrected a bad measurement of my own before concluding from it: the first probe showed resolve-index emitting 0 stderr lines with a duplicate planted, which would have contradicted the ticket. The probe was wrong, not the code -- resolve-index resolves from repoRoot and ignores BRAIN_MEMORY_TEST_ROOT (cli.mjs:170), so it had read the real store, which #636 had just reconciled to zero. That missing seam is recorded as a residual.

Six mutations red. M6 is the one that matters: it adds a FUTURE line with 2>&1 that this ticket never wrote, proving the guard covers the next author. Its first attempt did not land -- the perl pattern needed multiline mode -- and a mutation that fails to land produces a green run indistinguishable from a passing test, so it was rebuilt rather than reported.
